description: Four-column composite figure of the R650 steel in which each column pairs a bright-field TEM micrograph of a carbide (with a selected-area electron diffraction inset in b-d) with four EDS elemental maps laid out Al/C on the upper row and Mn/Cr on the lower row. (a) shows dark elongated rod-like and blocky carbides in a bright ferrite matrix, scale bar 125 nm, no SAED inset. (b) shows a long lath/lamellar carbide with a SAED inset labelled M3C [2 0 1-], indexed spots, 5 1/nm scale bar; micrograph scale bar 125 nm. (c) shows a rectangular blocky carbide with a SAED inset labelled M23C6 [1 1 0], 5 1/nm scale bar; micrograph scale bar 50 nm. (d) shows rounded/spheroidal carbides with a SAED inset whose indices are only partly readable (the caption assigns MC); micrograph scale bar 50 nm. In all four map sets, the C (yellow) and Mn (orange-brown) maps are bright in exactly the region occupied by the dark carbide, Cr (green) shows only faint enrichment, and Al (blue) shows no localised enrichment.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph (125 nm scale bar) showing dark elongated rod-like and small blocky carbides dispersed in a bright matrix; no SAED inset. Below it, four EDS maps (Al, C, Mn, Cr) in which C and Mn are enriched in the carbide-shaped dark regions.

TEM micrograph (125 nm scale bar) of a long lath/lamellar carbide with a diffraction spot inset labelled M3C [2 0 1-] and a 5 1/nm scale bar; the four EDS maps show strong C and Mn enrichment following the elongated carbide.

TEM micrograph (50 nm scale bar) showing a single rectangular blocky carbide with a SAED inset labelled M23C6 [1 1 0] and a 5 1/nm scale bar; EDS maps show C and Mn enrichment in the blocky feature with weaker Cr signal and no Al enrichment.

TEM micrograph (50 nm scale bar) showing rounded/spheroidal carbides; the SAED inset is present with a 5 1/nm scale bar but its indices and phase label are only partially legible (caption assigns MC). EDS maps show C and Mn enrichment in the rounded features.
Sixteen EDS maps in total, four per column, labelled Al (blue), C (yellow), Mn (orange-brown) and Cr (green); carbide regions are consistently C- and Mn-rich, weakly Cr-enriched and not Al-enriched.

observations.observation: The figure is composite: four TEM micrographs of the R650 steel, three of them carrying an SAED spot-pattern inset, each accompanied by four EDS elemental maps (Al, C, Mn, Cr).
Micrograph scale bars are printed as 125 nm in columns (a) and (b) and as 50 nm in columns (c) and (d).
The SAED insets in (b), (c) and (d) each carry a 5 1/nm reciprocal-space scale bar.
The inset of (b) is labelled M3C [2 0 1-] with individually indexed diffraction spots.
The inset of (c) is labelled M23C6 [1 1 0].
Panel (a) contains no SAED inset; only the micrograph and its four EDS maps are present.
Carbide morphology differs between columns: elongated rod/lath shapes in (a) and (b), a single rectangular blocky carbide in (c), and rounded or spheroidal particles in (d).
In every EDS map set the C and Mn maps are brightest exactly where the dark carbide sits, indicating co-localised C and Mn enrichment in the carbide.
The Al maps show a uniform, featureless background with no localised enrichment at the carbide positions.
The Cr maps show only faint, diffuse enrichment compared with the strong C and Mn signals.
The caption states the figure shows TEM micrographs, SAED patterns and EDS results of the R650 steel with (a) Carbides, (b) M3C, (c) M23C6 and (d) MC.
The citing text states that diffraction pattern calibration confirms the existence of MC, M23C6 and M7C3 carbides, whereas the caption labels panel (b) as M3C - the two readings do not fully agree.

The citing text states that the carbides are mainly concentrated outside the delta-ferrite lamellae, accumulating in the original martensite regions as products of element enrichment after martensite fragmentation.
The citing text states that massive carbide formation causes new ferrite to form in the adjacent low-carbon regions, producing composite lamellae of carbides dispersed in a ferrite matrix.
